<!-- WARNING: knitr RUNS chunks and inline code even inside an HTML comment
     like this one. Use #| eval: false to disable one. -->
<!-- One table = one chunk with a tbl-* label and its legend in #| tbl-cap.
     Cite it from the text with @tbl-models.
     Quarto writes the caption: do NOT also use flextable::set_caption() or it
     will be duplicated. -->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-models
#| include: true
#| tbl-cap: "Legend of table 1."
# flextable when the table needs formatting: rules, footnotes, grouping.
#
# The three rules a scientific table wants are drawn here rather than left to
# the Word template: none on top, one under the header row and one under the
# table. `hline_top(width = 0)` is what removes the default top rule.
#
# fit_flextable_to_page() is autofit() plus a ceiling: the table keeps the
# width its content needs and is only brought back in if it would run off the
# page. Do NOT stretch a table to the width of the line -- Quarto puts it in a
# container 5.5 inches wide, and a wider table comes out of Word misaligned.
tab <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("Treatment", "Altitude"),
  Estimate = c(0.42, -0.13),
  SE       = c(0.11, 0.05),
  p        = c(0.002, 0.014)
)
rule <- fp_border_default(style = "solid", color = "black", width = 1)

flextable(tab) |>
  align(part = "all", align = "left") |>
  hline_top(border = fp_border_default(width = 0), part = "all") |>
  hline_bottom(border = rule, part = "all") |>
  # The stars go in the p column as a suffix, so p stays a number and is
  # formatted rather than pasted together as text.
  colformat_double(j = "p", digits = 3, suffix = stars_pval(tab$p)) |>
  add_footer_lines("*p ≤ 0.05, **p ≤ 0.01, ***p ≤ 0.001") |>
  fit_flextable_to_page()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| include: true
#| tbl-cap: "Legend of table 2."
# knitr::kable() is enough for a simple table and travels better across
# formats, at the price of the formatting above: pandoc gives it columns of
# equal width and the Word template's `Table` style draws its rules.
knitr::kable(head(iris, 3))
```
